FINDING_ID: GPT5_DR_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: The documented “ascending abstraction guard” is not implemented in `stop()`. The class docstring, `_abstraction_dropping()` docstring, and comments repeatedly state that diminishing-returns should include an abstraction-drop factor conjunctively, but `stop()` ignores `_abstraction_dropping(round_idx)` entirely and returns true on any of the three exhaustion signals alone. This is not just dead code: it changes termination semantics from “signals gated by abstraction descent” to “ungated OR-stop,” making the detector materially more aggressive than specified.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Implement the guard explicitly in `stop()`, e.g. require `(signal_exhausted) and _abstraction_dropping(round_idx)` if that is the intended conjunctive policy, or update all docs/comments and remove `_abstraction_dropping()` if the guard was intentionally dropped. Add tests covering cases where `mu`/novelty are low but abstraction is flat or rising.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: GPT5_DR_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: `add_round_from_findings()` computes novelty against `self._all_prior_findings`, which is mutated incrementally and order-sensitively, but there is no enforcement that rounds are added in monotone `round_idx` order or only once. If a caller adds round 3 before round 2, or overwrites an earlier round, novelty and vocabulary state become historically inconsistent and cannot be recomputed from indexed data. The detector stores some data keyed by round, but novelty/vocabulary are maintained as append-only global state, so the object is not robust to out-of-order or corrected round ingestion.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Enforce strictly increasing unseen `round_idx` in `add_round()` / `add_round_from_findings()` and reject duplicates, or store per-round findings and recompute derived cumulative novelty/vocabulary from sorted rounds whenever state changes. Document ordering as a hard precondition if retained.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: GPT5_DR_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `add_round()` and `add_model_round()` accept physically invalid inputs without validation: negative `cost`, negative `yield_value`, and abstraction indices outside the nominal [0,1] range. Downstream behavior becomes nonsensical: negative cost can produce negative `mu` sign inversions or force the `c_r <= epsilon_cost` branch; negative yield can fabricate decreasing cumulative yield; out-of-range abstraction can inflate or invert yield calculations. This area relies on metric semantics but does not defend them at the API boundary.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `cost >= 0`, `yield_value >= 0`, and `0 <= mean_abstraction_new <= 1`; in `add_model_round()`, validate each finding’s `abstraction_index` similarly. Raise `ValueError` on violation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: GPT5_DR_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: `vocab_saturated()` has an off-by-one minimum-round bug. For a sustained window of length `W`, the code returns `False` when `round_idx < W`, but the first full window over zero-based rounds is available at `round_idx == W - 1`. As written, the detector refuses to evaluate saturation until one round later than necessary. Example: with `W=5`, rounds 0..4 already provide 5 observations, but the function still returns `False` at round 4 and only starts checking at round 5.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change the guard to `if round_idx < W - 1: return False`. Add tests for `W=1` and `W=5` boundary behavior.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: GPT5_DR_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: The area-level saturation logic uses `str(f.flaw_class)` as an “area proxy,” but `flaw_class` in the findings corpus is a defect taxonomy code, not the reviewed artifact area. That conflates orthogonal dimensions: the same review area can emit multiple flaw classes, and the same flaw class can appear across different areas. As a result, `vocab_saturated()` may conclude that “all active areas are saturated” when it has actually partitioned by error type rather than module/area, defeating the stated Exp14 fix for decomposed per-area dispatch.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Track a real `area_id` / module identifier on `Finding` and key `_area_vocab*` off that. If unavailable, disable per-area saturation and fall back to global vocab rather than silently using `flaw_class` as a surrogate.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: GPT5_DR_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: `vocab_saturated()` can declare saturation for an area after a single low-growth active round within the window. The comment explicitly justifies `len(area_rounds_in_window) < 1` as the threshold, meaning one sparse revisit to an area is enough to mark it saturated “from its perspective.” This is a very weak persistence criterion relative to the rest of the detector’s smoothing/persistence design and makes the stop decision highly sensitive to one anomalous area revisit. The implementation may match the comment, but the criterion undercuts the intended “sustained” concept in the method docstring.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Require at least 2 active observations for an area within the considered horizon, or define persistence in terms of the last `k` active visits to that area rather than mere presence in the global window. Update docstring to match the actual persistence rule.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: GPT5_DR_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.54  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: `remaining_value_estimate()` uses `avg_cost = mean(self._round_costs.values())` even when the detector is operating in per-model mode and `smoothed_marginal_value()` is derived from `aggregate_per_model_mu()`. That mixes incompatible estimators: numerator dynamics come from “best active model” marginal productivity, while projected future cost comes from historical system-level costs. Under attrition or dispatch resizing, the forecast can be directionally wrong. This is a model inconsistency inside the same area.  
PROPOSED_FIX: When per-model data exists, estimate future value using a consistent per-model forecast basis: e.g. active-model expected cost, selected aggregation policy, or explicit caller-supplied future cost schedule. Otherwise document that the estimate is only a coarse heuristic.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: GPT5_DR_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.46  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: `add_model_round()` allows the same `(model_id, round_idx)` to be written multiple times, silently overwriting prior cumulative yield/cost for that round while later rounds may already depend on the overwritten value as their `prev_yield` seed. This makes historical per-model trajectories non-idempotent and non-recomputing: updating round 1 after round 3 was added does not propagate to rounds 2..3.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either reject duplicate `(model_id, round_idx)` entries, or store raw per-round findings and recompute cumulative per-model yields for that model from sorted rounds upon overwrite.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: GPT5_DR_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.44  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: The API contract around `yield_value` vs. `add_round_from_findings()` is under-specified and easy to misuse. `add_round()` expects a cumulative yield `Y^(<=r)`, while `add_model_round()` derives and stores cumulative yield internally from per-round findings, and `add_round_from_findings()` accepts both cumulative and new findings. This mixed cumulative/incremental API shape makes accidental double-cumulation plausible, especially for callers integrating both methods.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rename parameters to make cumulative semantics explicit (`cumulative_yield_value`), or split the APIs into clearly incremental vs cumulative entry points with invariant checks. Add doc examples showing correct usage.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: GPT5_DR_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.41  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: [CROSS-COMPONENT, UNVERIFIED FROM THIS SCOPE] This detector keys all history by `round_idx` and assumes that index denotes iterative verification rounds. Prior FSM findings indicate `current_round = 0` is ambiguous across BLIND and SYNTH phases. If `DynamicManager` feeds both non-iterative phases and iterative rounds into this detector using the same index namespace, diminishing-returns metrics could be contaminated by non-comparable phases or overwritten at round 0. The risk is credible from interfaces but cannot be confirmed within this area alone.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Ensure the manager only records iterative review rounds here, or namespace phase/round identifiers explicitly. Add an assertion or phase parameter to detector ingestion methods.  
VERIFIED: FALSE
